stories.headline: Trump deploys extra aircraft carrier and warns Iran of 'big mistakes' as Kuwait drone strike kills two Italians
stories.standfirst: The US president said Washington would target the uninspected Pickaxe Mountain site near Natanz if strikes resume, while Tehran denied launching the Kuwait drones.
body: Speaking during Thanksgiving calls with US troops from Mar-a-Lago on Thursday 26 November, President Donald Trump said Washington had reinforced its Middle East naval presence and warned Tehran against further escalation. Iran International reports Trump told service members that victory was at hand, adding: 'We sent an extra aircraft carrier there. We're loaded up.' He said Iran was making big mistakes and questioned whether its leaders would accept a deal.

Trump told reporters he had spoken with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in recent days and warned that renewed US strikes would target Pickaxe Mountain, an underground complex near the Natanz uranium enrichment site that International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors have never visited. He said US forces enforcing the naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz had fired 150 missiles against threats to commercial shipping, while Patriot air-defence batteries had intercepted 560 missiles and drones since deploying in March under Operation Epic Fury. Trump also asserted after meeting NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte on Wednesday that NATO was now involved in Iran, without giving details.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Thursday that Qatari and Pakistani mediators were exchanging proposals between Washington and Tehran, but Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz — lifting the US blockade, unfreezing assets and halting hostilities — remained unchanged. Washington has insisted on upfront nuclear commitments from Tehran.

Separately, falling debris from intercepted drones hit a Kuwaiti military air-defence detection site on Thursday, killing two Italian Rheinmetall Italia technicians and wounding a Kuwaiti army captain and a Pakistani national, CNN and Anadolu Agency report. Italy's ANSA news agency identified the dead as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, who were maintaining Skyguard radar antennas. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said investigators found the drones were Iranian-built, noting regional pro-Iranian militias operate them, while Kuwait condemned a 'blatant violation of the sovereignty of the State of Kuwait'. Araghchi denied Iranian involvement and offered a joint inquiry, while an Iranian military spokesman alleged a false-flag operation.

stories.headline: Nvidia orders Dell and Supermicro to halt AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian nations
stories.standfirst: Shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia are paused while manufacturers navigate new US export-control rules targeting remote Chinese cloud access.
body: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners including Dell Technologies and Super Micro Computer to stop shipping AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it assesses compliance with new US Commerce Department export restrictions, TechCrunch and Malay Mail report, citing the Wall Street Journal and the Financial Times.

Both reports state it remains unclear whether the freeze is temporary or structural. The US rules, introduced last week, aim to close a loophole allowing Chinese AI developers to rent restricted Nvidia compute remotely through offshore data centres; TechCrunch cites an Institute for Progress estimate that such clusters supply roughly 24 per cent of China's AI computing power. Under the new framework, regional cloud providers face a 90-day clock to obtain export licences verifying that restricted Chinese entities are excluded from their customer lists.

A regional cloud executive told the Financial Times there was 'this new rule but no guidance on execution', describing compliance across the sector as chaotic. Malay Mail reports lenders have already withheld about $500m in credit facilities from Singapore cloud firm Aolani, jeopardising compute lease agreements with ByteDance. Nvidia recorded $104bn in 2025 revenue through its Singapore subsidiary — up 72 per cent year-on-year, reflecting regional billing for Taiwan and China — and moved aggressively to enforce the rules despite Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive this week.

stories.headline: EU leaders postpone €45bn Ukraine loan and long-term budget decision after Brussels clashes
stories.standfirst: Slovakia, Hungary and Czechia resisted Germany's demand that all 27 states join the 2027 loan, pushing talks to December.
body: European Union leaders ended Thursday's extraordinary Brussels summit without agreement on a proposed €45bn (£38bn) 2027 loan for Ukraine or the bloc's 2028–2034 budget, deferring a final decision until the 17–18 December European Council meeting, Ukrainska Pravda and The Guardian report. Proposed by the European Commission on 18 November alongside €45bn already scheduled under an earlier €90bn facility, the limited-recourse loan allocates €25bn for military assistance and €20bn for civilian needs.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted all 27 members must participate — telling reporters the union 'consists of 27 member states, not 23 or 24' — and threatened to veto the seven-year budget otherwise. Net-recipient holdouts Slovakia, Hungary and Czechia sought opt-outs: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico accused Merz of blackmail, while Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš demanded cohesion funding be separated from Ukraine aid. Bulgaria's Rumen Radev reversed his opposition on Thursday, offering to join the €20bn non-military component.

Germany also wants future EU Ukraine funding shifted from unanimity to majority voting before France's spring 2027 presidential election, where National Rally leader Marine Le Pen leads polls. On the wider 2028–2034 budget, The Guardian cites Council President António Costa's €1.78tn compromise — 10 per cent below the Commission's €2tn draft — whereas The Irish Times puts the figure at €1.5tn; Costa separately proposed a dedicated mechanism outside the €100bn Ukraine Reserve to cover €45bn to €55bn in debt-servicing interest.

stories.headline: Trump alters NATO joint statement to warn Ukraine against expanding war after urging Putin pullback
stories.standfirst: Hours after agreeing text targeting only Russia with Mark Rutte, the US president posted an edited version adding Kyiv ahead of next week's NATO ministerial.
body: US President Donald Trump unilaterally altered a joint statement agreed with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte following their 25 November meeting at Mar-a-Lago, adding Ukraine to a warning against actions that expand the war, the Kyiv Independent and UNN report, citing Politico. The official text issued by the White House and NATO urged Russia to avoid intentional or unintentional escalation, before Trump posted an amended version on Truth Social inserting 'and Ukraine'.

An anonymous NATO official confirmed to Politico that both sides had agreed only to the original wording naming Russia; the White House declined to comment. In a separate post on Thursday 26 November, The Guardian reports Trump said he had used talks with Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on 19 November to press the Russian president to 'pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe' to enable a rapid peace settlement.

The diverging messages precede a 2 December NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Brussels, with Washington having postponed releasing its European troop-posture review. Tensions over geographical spillover escalated this week after Ukraine confirmed sinking the Russian corvette Merkury off Benghazi, Libya, on 23 November alongside recent Russian airspace violations in Poland, prompting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul to warn against widening the conflict.

stories.headline: FCC grants conditional licence for SpaceX's one-million-satellite Starmind orbital AI data centres
stories.standfirst: The Space Bureau rejected astronomy and rival objections on radio-frequency grounds but deferred SpaceX's heliocentric disposal waiver above 600 km.
body: The US Federal Communications Commission's Space Bureau granted partial, conditional approval on 25 November for SpaceX's Starmind constellation of up to one million orbital AI data-centre satellites, roughly 89 times SpaceX's current fleet of about 11,200 active Starlink craft. Spaceflight Now and Quartz report the 50 km orbital shells span altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km at 30-degree and sun-synchronous inclinations.

Built in Bastrop, Texas, in partnership with Nvidia, each spacecraft features a 75-metre wingspan and 30-metre height, delivering roughly 250 kW — comparable to an NVL72 compute rack in orbit, according to SpaceX executive Michael Nicholls. Tightly formed clusters of around 10 satellites will link via 10 Tbps optical interconnects, while the FCC authorised Ka-band spectrum (18.8–19.3 GHz downlink and 28.6–29.1 GHz uplink) solely on an unprotected, non-interference basis for fallback telemetry, tracking and command.

SpaceX must deploy one satellite by 25 November 2033, 10 per cent by 2035, 50 per cent by 2038 and all one million by 2040 under the 15-year licence, though Elon Musk targeted first Starship-launched deployments in Q3 2027. The FCC dismissed petitions from Amazon Leo, Viasat and the American Astronomical Society — which said it was 'disheartened and dismayed' over optical-astronomy impacts — as outside spectrum jurisdiction, but deferred SpaceX's waiver to dispose of spacecraft into heliocentric orbits, requiring a modified debris plan before operating above 600 km.

stories.headline: England NHS hospitals brace for winter flu surge as admissions jump 79 per cent to pre-Covid high
stories.standfirst: UKHSA week 48 data put weekly influenza admissions at 8.98 per 100,000 while NHS England chief Jim Mackey urges masks and condemns corridor care.
body: Weekly influenza hospital admissions in England climbed nearly 79 per cent in seven days to 8.98 per 100,000 people, up from 5.03 the previous week, according to UK Health Security Agency week 48 surveillance data published on 26 November covering the period to 22 November. The Guardian reports this is the highest late-November flu admission rate since before the Covid-19 pandemic, even as overall flu circulation remains classed as moderate.

UKHSA recorded ICU and HDU flu admissions rising from 0.16 to 0.28 per 100,000, laboratory positivity reaching 17.8 per cent on 22 November and GP swab positivity hitting 21.1 per cent. Covid-19 and RSV admissions remain low at 2.96 and 2.34 per 100,000. Flu vaccine uptake trails last winter across every tracked group except pregnant women (34.9 per cent versus 33.9 per cent), standing at 67.6 per cent among over-65s, 34.1 per cent in under-65 clinical risk groups and 39.2 per cent for two- and three-year-olds.

Addressing an NHS Alliance conference in London on Thursday, NHS England chief executive Jim Mackey warned of a 'horrible spike' within five to 10 days, urged hospital leaders to consider asking staff and visitors to wear masks, and criticised the normalisation of corridor care. Trusts in Nottingham, Derby and Burton, Kettering and Northampton, and Nottinghamshire declared critical incidents this week, after Health Service Journal figures showed 38 per cent of A&E patients at Nottingham University Hospitals faced corridor waits between August and October.

stories.headline: Ofcom orders BBC iPlayer and UK public broadcasters into top nine smart TV app slots
stories.standfirst: The final Media Act 2024 code of practice covers 15 connected-TV platforms including Apple TV, Fire TV, Samsung and LG, though hardware remotes stay exempt.
body: Ofcom published its final statement, Code of Practice and statutory guidance under the Media Act 2024 on 26 November, defining what constitutes an 'appropriate degree of prominence' for public service broadcasters across connected televisions and streaming devices. The rules govern 15 designated platforms including Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV, Android TV, Google TV, LG webOS, Samsung Tizen, Roku, Hisense VIDAA, Sky Q and Entertainment OS, Virgin Media Horizon and TiVo, YouView and Freely.

Under the Code, platforms seeking safe-harbour compliance must display BBC iPlayer, ITVX, Channel 4, Channel 5, S4C Clic and STV Player without scrolling inside the first nine tiles of the main app row, adjusted regionally for Wales and Scotland. Live streaming guides must place BBC One first through STV seventh, text and voice search must rank relevant public service shows above paid promotions, and platforms must add disability accessibility tools including voice guidance, magnification and clearer subtitle labels.

Cord Busters reports Ofcom testing found STV Player and S4C Clic currently sit at median positions 17th and 23rd. Existing televisions running platform software released from July 2025 onward fall within scope, despite objections from Samsung, LG and Google over retrospective updates, while remote-control shortcut buttons, YouTube and mobile apps remain excluded. Broadcasters warned that awaiting secondary legislation, app designations and a 12-to-18-month implementation window could delay changes until 2028.

stories.headline: Anthropic details zero-downtime Claude Messages API migration from Python to Rust
stories.standfirst: Claude wrote the core request path in a week, but matching live traffic required shadowed checkpoint fingerprints and three agent verification loops.
body: Anthropic published an engineering post on 25 November detailing how it migrated its core Messages API — serving external developers, Claude Code and Cowork — from Python to Rust with zero downtime and no feature freeze, cutting CPU usage per request by roughly 70 per cent and median time to first token on Claude Code traffic by about 20 per cent, while InfoWorld and PC Guide report memory consumption fell by more than 80 per cent. With API volume up roughly 1,800-fold between early 2024 and autumn 2026, an earlier incremental Rust output parser trimmed CPU by only 8 to 10 per cent while forcing each token across the Python-Rust boundary three times.

Although Claude generated the initial Rust request path in roughly a week, Anthropic engineers wrote that 'Verification, not generation, had become the bottleneck.' By April, the Rust service passed about 98 per cent of roughly 700 ported integration tests yet matched only around 25 per cent of live production inputs; an audit uncovered over 100 weakened test assertions and combinatorial edge cases across dozens of flags, such as Python escaping emojis in JSON tool calls differently from Rust.

To verify parity without reading user payloads or double-billing customers, Anthropic shadowed production requests, replayed single model completions to Rust to isolate nondeterminism, and logged privacy-preserving structural checkpoints with byte-offset and length fingerprints. Automated scripts batched novel fingerprints every 10 to 30 minutes to a coordinating Claude agent and worker sandboxes running sub-second local input checks and scripted-model output comparisons. Human engineers gated PR promotion between the inner sandbox loop and outer production shadow A/B comparisons, while a memory loop codified review corrections into CLAUDE.md rules, lints and cross-language merge checks before September's full cutover.

stories.headline: Google Play to publish solo commercial developers' home addresses worldwide from March 2027
stories.standfirst: All active Play Console accounts must declare trader status under EEA and UK consumer laws by 1 February 2027 or risk global app removal.
body: Google Play Console policies require every active developer account worldwide to declare 'trader' or 'non-trader' status under European Economic Area and UK consumer legislation by 1 February 2027, ahead of Google Play shifting to an online marketplace model in those regions on 1 March 2027. Failure to declare risks update blocks and global app removal, while misrepresenting commercial activity violates the EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and the UK Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act.

Under European Commission criteria cited by Google, developers earning regular remuneration from paid downloads, in-app purchases or ad-supported apps qualify as traders unless they cease distributing in the EEA and UK. From 1 March 2027, Google will show trader contact details, D-U-N-S numbers and terms-of-service links to Play Store users globally, rather than restricting visibility to Europe; EEA and UK listings will also replace Google with the trader's name in the 'Offered by' field.

For personal developer accounts, Google's help page warns: 'Be aware that your address will also be publicly displayed' alongside a contact phone number. The Next Web and MLQ.ai report Google draws the address from verified payments profiles and rejects PO boxes — unlike Apple, which displays EU trader details only within the EU and permits documented PO boxes — prompting solo developers to warn of physical safety risks for home-based creators.

stories.headline: Piastri confirms Lusail driver-steward talks on 2026 penalties as Norris reflects on McLaren slump
stories.standfirst: McLaren enters Qatar nine points behind Red Bull for third in the Constructors' Championship ahead of Friday practice under Lusail's 27-lap stint cap.
body: McLaren driver Oscar Piastri confirmed during Thursday's FIA press conference at Lusail that Formula 1 drivers were meeting stewards and FIA officials on Thursday evening to review 2026 racing guidelines and penalty consistency, telling reporters: 'We have a meeting about it tonight.' Grande Prêmio reports discussions cover wheel-to-wheel incidents shaped by 2026 electrical energy deployment differences, including Piastri's clash with Arvid Lindblad in Mexico, though no guideline changes have been announced.

With Mercedes and Kimi Antonelli having already sealed both 2026 titles, McLaren sits nine points behind Red Bull for third in the Constructors' Championship with two rounds left after Lando Norris (P2) and Piastri (P3) scored 33 points in Las Vegas. Reigning 2025 champion Norris — a three-time winner with four poles this season — told Formula1.com that 2026 has 'certainly not been our finest' year following early setbacks under the new regulations, and told RacingNews365 the team would revisit its 2025 Lusail lap-seven safety-car strategy error in pre-weekend meetings.

Seventh-placed Piastri, nearly 100 points behind Norris, told Auto Action his struggles centred on MCL40 handling and tyre behaviour rather than the power unit, adding that Pirelli's 27-lap maximum stint cap across the 57-lap standard-format race could mean largely flat-out stints. Elsewhere in Thursday's FIA briefing, Red Bull's Isack Hadjar confirmed reinforced front wings after his Las Vegas failure, while Mercedes's George Russell blamed a missed inside braking-point bump reference for hitting Antonelli.

today: Friday 27 November: Qatar Grand Prix practice at Lusail (FP1 13:30, FP2 17:00 UK time); noon deadline for Gordon Brothers' Mark Newton-Jones to respond to Commons Business Committee chair Liam Byrne.
Saturday 28 – Sunday 29 November: Qatar Grand Prix FP3 (Sat 14:30), qualifying (Sat 18:00) and 57-lap race (Sun 16:00 UK time, 27-lap maximum tyre stint).
Sunday 29 November: EU Euro 7 vehicle emissions rules apply to new car and van type-approvals, setting first-ever brake-particle (3 mg/km EV, 7 mg/km others) and EV battery durability limits.
Tuesday 1 December: Scheduled Chapter 11 bankruptcy auction for Character.AI's platform and 21 million user chat histories, opposed by 42 US states and DC.

Wednesday 2 – Sunday 6 December: NATO foreign ministers meet in Brussels (2 Dec); EU competition ministers consider Ireland's 'Made in Europe' UK car assembly compromise (3 Dec); Gadi Eisenkot's 28-day Israeli coalition mandate expires (6 Dec, extendable by 14 days).

briefs.text: Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee chair Liam Byrne wrote to Gordon Brothers executive Mark Newton-Jones on 26 November, setting a noon 27 November deadline to schedule a public hearing and seeking assurances no Gordon Brothers affiliate will act in an insolvency capacity over Poundland.

The UK government has again delayed publishing its long-awaited National Cyber Action Plan — structured around Threat, Growth and Resilience pillars — from mid-November to 9 December, drawing criticism from House of Lords National Resilience Committee member Baroness Northover.

S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA credit rating on CreditWatch Negative for a 90-day review on 25 November, citing board-governance and key-man risks after Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement and warning a cut to AA- could raise guarantee costs on its $500bn AI financing programme.

Mozilla Firefox head Ajit Varma told Business Insider that security fixes now absorb 27 per cent of Firefox engineering effort, up from about 10 per cent a year ago, as Anthropic's Mythos (271 bugs in April) and OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber (81 bugs) surface complex vulnerabilities faster.

Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party struck a coalition deal with Yair Golan's Democrats on 26 November covering the internal security and communications ministries — lifting Eisenkot to 36 of 61 seats — alongside reports of Haredi student draft-exemption concessions as talks with Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad were cancelled.

The EU's Euro 7 vehicle emissions rules (Regulation 2024/1257) take effect for new car and van type-approvals on Sunday 29 November, introducing 3 mg/km EV and 7 mg/km combustion brake-dust limits and 80 per cent five-year EV battery durability rules, with Great Britain mandating compliance for new registrations from November 2027.
